result.title: Target-Consistent Action Guidance via Semi-Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Drifting World Models
result.summary: Action-conditioned world models let robots imagine the outcomes of their actions for planning and offline policy evaluation, but these uses need many rollouts, which multi-step diffusion makes expensive. Drifting models move the iteration from inference to training and generate samples in one network pass. DriftWorld brought this paradigm to action-conditioned world models; to strengthen action following, it repels predictions from the current frame, a construction borrowed from classifier-free guidance. We show that this accentuation has a target bias: the push persists even when a prediction matches the recorded future, in kernel, balanced, and unbalanced Wasserstein drifting fields alike. We introduce Mass-Share Accentuation (MSA) to remove this bias. MSA treats the current frame as a counterfactual destination competing with the recorded future in a semi-relaxed optimal transport problem; subtracting the closed-form share of the correct future makes the guidance vanish at the target, and the remainder is shared by all predictions. We prove that the recorded future is the unique fixed point along the motion direction for collapsed predictions, and that the guidance fades with prediction error. On Push-T, Robomimic, and BridgeV2, where trained models under-react rather than overshoot, MSA improves action ranking, response slope, and moving-region error over latent-space baselines at no inference cost, though these benchmarks do not isolate bias removal as the cause.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析动作条件漂移式世界模型中沿用 classifier-free guidance 的「推离当前帧」引导存在目标偏差：即使预测已命中记录未来仍持续施力；提出 Mass-Share Accentuation，把当前帧视作与记录未来在半松弛最优传输中竞争的反事实目标，用闭式份额扣除使引导在目标处归零，并证明记录未来为唯一不动点、引导随预测误差衰减，在 Push-T、Robomimic、BridgeV2 上评测动作排序与响应斜率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「引导在匹配证据时应消失」的不动点构造与闭式纠偏，可供核查是否用于 LVR 中视觉证据加权和 latent 状态更新时的过冲/欠响应与目标偏差问题；但论文属机器人世界模型，未涉及 latent visual reasoning 本身，迁移需较多判断。
